newsitem.title: USA: GM anxious to settle Oklahoma plant strike.
newsitem.headline: GM anxious to settle Oklahoma plant strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp Chairman John Smith said Monday the automaker was anxious to resume production at its striking Oklahoma car plant.
"We're anxious to get that plant back online," Smith said. "We have to negotiate a way through some tough business issues."

Speaking to a luncheon of business executives, Smith said it was too early to assess the impact of the 11-day strike, but said production of its new mid-size Malibu had been affected. He said the company had high expectations for the Malibu model.
Smith would not say if Monday's positive earnings report for its Delphi unit would speed a planned initial public offering.
"The first thing we need to do is integrate our Delco Electronics operation that is now part of Hughes into Delphi. And that depends on the sale to Raytheon," Smith said.
Smith said the automaker's profits from international operations were disappointing, "but we knew going in that there's a tough market and there's overcapacity."
"The economies are not strong (in Europe) and we're seeing a lot of price pressure in the marketplace," Smith said.
